title: Grid, Random & Bayesian Hyperparameter Search
interviewAnswer: Hyperparameter tuning searches settings not learned directly by model fitting. Random search is often more efficient than exhaustive grids in high-dimensional spaces; Bayesian optimization helps when evaluations are expensive.
keyPoints: Tune using validation/CV, never the final test set.

Parallelism and early stopping can reduce cost.
why: Grid, Random & Bayesian Hyperparameter Search is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
intuition: Tune using validation/CV, never the final test set.
deepDive: Hyperparameter tuning searches settings not learned directly by model fitting. Random search is often more efficient than exhaustive grids in high-dimensional spaces; Bayesian optimization helps when evaluations are expensive. Search spaces matter more than search algorithm in many cases. Parallelism and early stopping can reduce cost. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: Tune learning rate, depth and regularization with random search and keep the test set untouched until final selection.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.

lab.goal: Tune a model without touching the test set.
lab.buildIt:
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
X,y=make_classification(n_samples=700,n_features=10,n_informative=5,random_state=0)
Xtr,Xte,ytr,yte=train_test_split(X,y,test_size=.2,random_state=0,stratify=y)
lab.useIt:
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
gs=GridSearchCV(RandomForestClassifier(random_state=0),{'max_depth':[3,6,None],'min_samples_leaf':[1,5,15]},cv=4,scoring='roc_auc').fit(Xtr,ytr)
print(gs.best_params_,gs.best_score_,gs.score(Xte,yte))
lab.shipIt: Log the search space, folds, metric and winning configuration; keep the final test set isolated and cap tuning cost with sensible priors/search spaces.
